decisions.reason: Define-XML ADTTE.TRTDUR (native MT.ADTTE.TRTDUR, define-adam.xml line 5241) names ADSL.TRTDUR, but Define-XML ADSL lists only TRTDURD and the published ADSL has no TRTDUR column. The specification itself reads ADSL.TRTDURD at adtte_v2.yaml line 30, so the documented copy source is absent from the submission.

Define-XML ADTTE.ADT takes ASTDT only when it is after TRTSDT, but the adtte.r L48-L58 event source has no date test and relies on AOCC01FL, which adae.r L211-L220 sets among TRTEMFL records whose definition is the inclusive ASTDT >= TRTSDT. An event on the TRTSDT day is therefore an event in the program but not under the documented strict rule.

Define-XML ADTTE.ADT falls back to ADSL.RFENDTC, but adtte.r L72-L94 censors at EOS2DT, the DS disposition date, using RFENDTC only for deaths; its own comment at L79-L80 says this is not described in the specifications.

The literal probe applies the strict after-TRTSDT test of Define-XML ADTTE.ADT to the first treatment-emergent AOCC01FL dermatologic event of ADRG pages 11-12 and falls back to converted ADSL.RFENDTC; the 5 differing records are first events dated on TRTSDT, which ADT__INCLUSIVE (the >= of Define-XML ADAE.TRTEMFL) reproduces. ADT__PROGRAM is supported by adtte.r L48-L58, L72-L94 and L97-L104, which apply no after-TRTSDT test, and serves only as a reading of how the reference was computed.

AOCC01FL is flagged only on TRTEMFL=Y dermatologic records (adae.r L211-L220), so the adtte.r L48-L58 event source applies the TRTEMFL test of Define-XML ADTTE.CNSR to the first dermatologic event that the ADTTE.ADT and EVNTDESC methods describe. The program restates that rule; it does not compute CNSR differently.

Define-XML ADSL.RFENDT explicitly states "RFENDTC converted to SAS date", so ADTTE.ADT names the raw text input and its conversion while ADTTE.SRCVAR names that converted date. Read with ADSL.RFENDT, these are compatible stages of the documented lineage rather than contradictory rules.

adtte.r L48-L58 and L86-L94 write SRCVAR ASTDT for events and RFENDT for censored records, exactly the two values Define-XML ADTTE.SRCVAR lists for those branches. That the censor date is EOS2DT rather than RFENDT is the ADT departure already found in ADTTE.ADT.CR-8.9, not a different SRCVAR computation.

Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL subsets to CQ01NAM='' (an empty query name), while its own parenthetical and ADRG page 12 describe the flag as the first treatment-emergent dermatological event, and Define-XML ADAE.CQ01NAM sets DERMATOLOGIC EVENTS for those events and NULL otherwise. The two documents state contradictory selection conditions for the same flag.

Define-XML ADTTE.STARTDT (native MT.ADTTE.STARTDT, define-adam.xml line 5225) names ADSL.RFSTDTC, which Define-XML ADSL takes from DM.RFSTDTC, while adtte_v1.yaml line 166 reads ADSL.TRTSDT, which Define-XML ADSL takes from SV.SVSTDTC at visit 3. Agreement of the values on this submission does not make TRTSDT the documented source.

Define-XML ADTTE.ADT takes ADAE.ASTDT only when it occurred after TRTSDT, but adtte_v1.yaml lines 181-183 take FIRST_DERM.ASTDT whenever an AOCC01FL record exists. That record is bounded only by Define-XML ADAE.TRTEMFL (ASTDT >= TRTSDT), so events on TRTSDT itself pass and the strict boundary has no counterpart.

ADRG pages 11-12 state that the first treatment-emergent dermatologic event captured by CQ01NAM is flagged AOCC01FL to give ADTTE its traceability, so the dermatologic condition is carried by that flag. FIRST_DERM at adtte_v1.yaml line 69 selects ADAE.AOCC01FL = 'Y' and feeds ADT at lines 181-183, which is the counterpart; the separate wording conflict in Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL is ADTTE.SRCSEQ.CR-8.7.

Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL flags a record only within the TRTEMFL='Y' subset, so the first dermatologic record that FIRST_DERM selects at adtte_v1.yaml line 69 always has TRTEMFL='Y'. CNSR at lines 201-204 is 0 exactly when that treatment-emergent dermatologic event exists and 1 otherwise, which is Define-XML ADTTE.CNSR read for the event record of ADRG pages 11-12.

ADRG pages 11-12 state that the first treatment-emergent dermatologic event captured by CQ01NAM is flagged AOCC01FL to give ADTTE its traceability, so the dermatologic condition is carried by that flag. CNSR at adtte_v1.yaml lines 201-204 tests HAS_EVENT, which reads FIRST_DERM and its ADAE.AOCC01FL = 'Y' filter at line 69, the counterpart of that condition.

CNSR at adtte_v1.yaml lines 201-204 is 0 exactly when HAS_EVENT = 'Y' and 1 otherwise, so it takes no other value. Substituting that definition into Define-XML ADTTE.EVNTDESC gives the HAS_EVENT branches and both literal strings at lines 210-213, an equivalent expression of the documented rule.

Define-XML ADTTE.SRCDOM requires the domain that populates ADT, and SRCDOM at adtte_v1.yaml lines 219-222 branches on the same HAS_EVENT condition as ADT at lines 181-184, so it names ADAE exactly when ADT comes from FIRST_DERM.ASTDT. The missing strict after-TRTSDT test is a clause of the ADT rule, already raised as ADTTE.ADT.CR-6.1, not a separate SRCDOM condition.

ADRG pages 11-12 state that the first treatment-emergent dermatologic event captured by CQ01NAM is flagged AOCC01FL to give ADTTE its traceability, so the dermatologic condition is carried by that flag. SRCDOM at adtte_v1.yaml lines 219-222 branches on HAS_EVENT, which reads FIRST_DERM and its ADAE.AOCC01FL = 'Y' filter at line 69, the counterpart of that condition.

Define-XML ADTTE.SRCVAR requires the variable that populates ADT, and SRCVAR at adtte_v1.yaml lines 228-231 names ASTDT and RFENDT under the same HAS_EVENT branches that take FIRST_DERM.ASTDT and ADSL.RFENDT for ADT at lines 181-184. The missing strict after-TRTSDT test is a clause of the ADT rule, already raised as ADTTE.ADT.CR-6.1, not a separate SRCVAR condition.

ADRG pages 11-12 state that the first treatment-emergent dermatologic event captured by CQ01NAM is flagged AOCC01FL to give ADTTE its traceability, so the dermatologic condition is carried by that flag. SRCVAR at adtte_v1.yaml lines 228-231 branches on HAS_EVENT, which reads FIRST_DERM and its ADAE.AOCC01FL = 'Y' filter at line 69, the counterpart of that condition.

HAS_EVENT at adtte_v1.yaml lines 172-175 is 'Y' exactly when FIRST_DERM.AESEQ is not null, and SRCDOM at lines 219-222 is ADAE exactly then. FIRST_DERM.AESEQ at line 236 therefore equals ADAE.AESEQ when SRCDOM=ADAE and is null otherwise, an equivalent expression of Define-XML ADTTE.SRCSEQ.

ADRG pages 11-12 state that the first treatment-emergent dermatologic event captured by CQ01NAM is flagged AOCC01FL to give ADTTE its traceability, so the dermatologic condition is carried by that flag. SRCSEQ at adtte_v1.yaml line 236 copies AESEQ from FIRST_DERM, whose ADAE.AOCC01FL = 'Y' filter at line 69 is the counterpart of that condition.

Native define-adam.xml IT.ADTTE.STUDYID, lines 1820-1824, has def:Origin Type="Predecessor" with the description ADSL.STUDYID, which adtte_v1.yaml lines 78-82 carry; the section text omits that origin but the retained Define-XML states the derivation. The cited adtte.r L97-L104 is program code and does not decide documentation.

The record source is the all-subjects row rule at adtte_v1.yaml lines 243-246, one record per ADSL subject.
